| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Tool | kailash (category modules) |

| Time | ~10 min + a rebuild |
| Layer/Category | CLASSIC (+ any layer) |
| Tags | `getting-started`, `taxonomy`, `category`, `nixos` |


## Problem

The booted image carries the default tool set. The task: extend the
set — say the ATTACK A-2 category for LLM prompt-injection work —
while the declarative build stays intact. There is no `apt install`
on Kailash. Enabling a category is a configuration change that a
rebuild applies. The result is reproducible, and the change stays
reviewable.

## Solution

Find the category id. Enable it in the system configuration. Rebuild.
Verify:

```bash
# 1. Identify the category a tool belongs to
kailash info garak            # -> category: a-02-prompt-injection-jailbreaks

# 2. Add the enablement option to your system configuration
#    (configuration.nix or your host module), layer-scoped per the
#    category-module contract:
#
#    kailash.layers.attack.categories.a-02-prompt-injection-jailbreaks.enable = true;
#
#    (a `kailash enable <category>` helper that emits this snippet is
#     roadmap-stage — the landed CLI slice is list/search/info/
#     profile list/manifest validate; until it lands, write the
#     option path directly as above)

# 3. Rebuild and switch
sudo nixos-rebuild switch

# 4. Verify what the manifest declares for that category
kailash list --category a-02-prompt-injection-jailbreaks
```

What success looks like:

- the rebuild applies cleanly
- the category module's package list comes straight from the
  manifest — no hand-maintained package set
- `kailash list --category <cat-id>` returns the category's row
  inventory, and those tools are on the system's PATH
- a rebuild without changes reproduces the same tool set
  byte-for-byte (same lock)

## Discussion

- **One category = one module:** every category is a single module
  file. The module mounts its configuration from the manifest's
  package list. Enabling it is a declarative act over the four-layer,
  32-category taxonomy (CLASSIC / ATTACK / DEFENCE / OPS). The
  profiles use the same surface.
- **Safety classes still govern:** enabling a category does not
  flatten safety classes. `requires-target` tools (most of ATTACK)
  do not fire without an explicit target. `exp` rows
  (e.g. hexstrike-ai in A-7) install only via gate wrappers and stay
  double-keyed — see [Gate lab-mode and exp-classified
  tools](../admin/lab-mode-gating.html).
- **Data packs are NOT categories:** wordlists and corpus packs
  (seclists, pw-packs, the C-7 SDR pack) use opt-in `kailash-data.*`
  derivations. The packs stay excluded from every default image by
  construction. An enabled category never carries corpus packs — see
  [Refresh wordlists and data
  packs](../admin/data-packs.html).
- **Pick the target scope deliberately:** on Kailash, the profile
  statement (via image choice) plus the enabled categories expresses
  the intent. The build (flake lock) makes that intent exact.
